title: Structural mechanism governing the directionality of bridge recombination.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and parsed the structure file 9WHX.cif from the Protein Data Bank (1.77 MB, 14,677 atom records, 8 chains). Downloaded the whole GEO (Gene Expression Omnibus) deposit GSE328474_RAW.tar (133 KB) and listed it: 6 bigWig coverage tracks (5.8-32 KB each) from 3 RNA-seq samples. Queried NCBI for the series summary (n_samples = 3, E. coli). Queried the EMPIAR (Electron Microscopy Public Image Archive) application programming interface for EMPIAR-13446: 6,558 + 7,668 multi-frame TIFF micrographs at 5760x4092 pixels x 50 frames, i.e. multiple terabytes of raw images. Read the full open-access text and its data-availability statement.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The contents of Supplementary Table 1 ('Nucleic acids used in this study', i.e. the oligonucleotide sequences) and Supplementary Figs. 1-6 (the uncropped gel images). The Europe PMC supplementary-file endpoint timed out, so I never opened those files; I only have their captions from the article text. All recombination-efficiency numbers (gel densitometry, qPCR) are described in figure panels and were not retrieved as a table.

a1_downloadable.note: All deposits are open with no login: I pulled 9WHX.cif from the Protein Data Bank and the complete GEO archive GSE328474_RAW.tar directly. EMPIAR-13446 and the EMDB maps are also public.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: KILLER. There is no tabular dataset at all. The only quantity a model could predict - recombination (insertion/excision) efficiency - exists solely as bands on gels and bar charts inside figure panels; it would have to be constructed by densitometry on the Supplementary Fig. 6 gel images. No label column exists anywhere in the deposited files I opened.

a3_inputs_present.note: The bridge-RNA and DNA substrate sequences are listed in Supplementary Table 1 and in Extended Data Fig. 4, so inputs exist as sequences rather than accessions - but I could not retrieve that supplementary file (Europe PMC timed out), and they are not paired to any label.

a4_units_stated.note: No units column, because there is no table. The text reports efficiencies as percentages from gel quantification and as relative qPCR values; these are two different scales that are never tabulated together.

a5_enough_rows.note: Verified: the GEO series has exactly 3 RNA-seq samples (6 bigWig tracks). The structural data is 2 Protein Data Bank entries. The biochemistry covers roughly a dozen handshake-guide bridge-RNA variants in triplicate - far below the ~400-1,500 row floor.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~2 MB (one 1.77 MB structure file plus 133 KB of bigWig tracks)
a6_fits_laptop.note: The processed data is trivially small. The raw EMPIAR-13446 micrographs are multiple terabytes and would fail this check, but nobody would need them.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: What I opened matches the paper: data-availability names 9WHX/9WHY, EMD-65978/9, EMPIAR-13446 and GSE328474, and NCBI confirms 3 samples. (The text-mined accessions 8WT6-8WT8 belong to the earlier 2024 insertion-complex paper, as the text states.)

a8_label_provenance.note: Not a problem in principle: the candidate measurements (gel band fractions, qPCR of recombined junctions) are direct physical readouts, not another model's output. But since no label table exists, this check is moot.

backbone.name: RNA-FM (an RNA language model) or Evo 2 (a DNA/genome language model) could embed bridge-RNA and target-DNA sequences
backbone.hardware: CPU would suffice for the few dozen short sequences here, which is precisely the problem - there is nothing to fit a head on
backbone.licence: RNA-FM is MIT-licensed; not relevant given there are no labels

integration.partner_dataset: The bridge-RNA target/donor specificity libraries from Durrant et al., Nature 2024 (10.1038/s41586-024-07552-4), the paper this one builds on, which measured recombination across large sequence libraries
integration.join_key: Bridge-RNA target-binding-loop and donor-binding-loop guide sequence, plus the 2-nucleotide core and handshake-guide dinucleotides
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Does the geometry seen in these excision structures explain which guide-DNA pairings succeed in the earlier high-throughput library, i.e. can structure-derived features predict recombination efficiency better than base-pairing rules alone? - but all the data for that question lives in the 2024 paper, not this one.

controls.positive_control: None available: no held-out measurements exist in this deposit.
controls.external_validation: The Durrant 2024 bridge-RNA library would be the external set, but it would have to be the training set too, which makes this paper redundant.

honest_claim_h3: No predictive claim is possible from this paper's data; the only honest statement it supports is mechanistic - two cryo-EM structures show the excision substrates bind in a linear, X-shaped arrangement rather than the bent U-shape of insertion.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use bridge RNA and DNA sequence to predict how efficiently a programmable recombinase inserts or excises a DNA segment.
plain_idea.train_on: Each example would be a bridge-RNA guide sequence paired with its target and donor DNA sequences. This paper supplies only about a dozen handshake-guide variants (verified: 3 RNA-seq samples, 2 structures, no measurement table), so the training set would have to come from elsewhere.
plain_idea.predict: Percent recombination (insertion or excision), measured either by band intensity on a denaturing gel or by quantitative PCR across the recombined junction - both reported here only inside figure panels.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Genome-editing groups using bridge recombinases need to pick guide sequences that work; a sequence-to-efficiency model would cut the number of constructs they build and test. Nothing here supports building one.

ml_idea: The only sensible machine-learning idea in this area - predict bridge-recombinase insertion/excision efficiency from the bridge-RNA guide and DNA target/donor sequences, using an RNA or DNA language model as a frozen feature extractor - cannot be built from this paper. Its deposited data is two cryo-EM structures, 6 tiny bigWig coverage tracks, and terabytes of raw micrographs. The sequence-to-efficiency libraries live in the earlier Durrant et al. 2024 Nature paper; if that project is wanted, evaluate that paper instead.

effort.compute_note: Working set measured directly: 1.77 MB structure file plus a 133 KB GEO archive. No embedding or cross-validation estimates given because there is no labelled set to run them on.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the rows in any quantitative table attached to the paper. I did: there are none. The GEO deposit is 3 samples / 6 bigWig tracks totalling 133 KB, and the supplementary material is figures, a reporting summary and a list of oligonucleotides.

verdict_reason: Fails A2 and A5, both verified by opening the files. This is a cryo-EM mechanism paper: the deposits are 2 structures (9WHX/9WHY), terabytes of raw micrographs, and 3 RNA-seq samples as 6 bigWig tracks totalling 133 KB. The quantity worth predicting - recombination efficiency - exists only as gel bands and bar charts in figure panels, so the label would have to be constructed by densitometry on roughly a dozen variants. The interesting sequence-to-efficiency data belongs to the earlier Durrant et al. 2024 Nature paper, not this one.
